test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In how many years will a sum of Rs. 12,000 become Rs. 14,520 at a rate of 10% per annum on compound interest, compounded annually?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Using the ratio method: Principal (P) : Amount (A) = 12000 : 14520

Simplifying the ratio: P : A = 120 : 145.2 = 100 : 121

Since 100 : 121 = (10)² : (11)², which corresponds to (1 + 10%)², the time period is 2 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹12,000, Amount (A) = ₹14,520, Rate (R) = 10% per annum.

**Formula Used:** A = P × (1 + R/100)t, where t is the time in years.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d30931f601a78abc5e87f92435be3d064e325e6a931e10e31ca9ec9ab31740c6.png] 
**Calculations:**

→ 14520 = 12000 × (1 + 10/100)t

→ 14520 ÷ 12000 = (11/10)t

→ 1452 ÷ 1200 = (1.1)t

→ 121 ÷ 100 = (1.1)t

→ 1.21 = (1.1)t

→ (1.1)² = (1.1)t

⇒ t = 2 years

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount accumulated on principal P at rate R% compound interest per annum compounded annually for t years is given by A = P(1 + R/100)t.

Effective Rate of Interest

For a rate of 10% compounded annually, the effective rate for 2 years is calculated using successive percentage change: 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%.

13
